name: The Smiths
label: Rough Trade
lede: A 14-year-old guitarist knocked on a stranger's door in Stretford, and five years later the Smiths had made four studio albums, rewritten British guitar pop and broken up before the last one came out. The arguing over the money took longer.

hero.by: Sire Records publicity photo, 1984. Wikimedia Commons

eras.title: A knock on a door in Stretford
eras.text: Johnny Marr was a teenage guitarist with a borrowed idea: Jerry Leiber had turned up on Mike Stoller's doorstep, so he would turn up on Morrissey's. Inside a year the band had a name chosen for its plainness, a bassist from Marr's school and a drummer who auditioned on mushrooms.

years.h: Marr shows up unannounced at Morrissey's front door
years.p: Marr and his friend Steve Pomfret knock at Steven Morrissey's house in Stretford. The two had met at a Patti Smith gig in 1978, when Marr was 14; Marr was copying Jerry Leiber, who found Mike Stoller the same way.
years.xp:
Marr remembered it as a sunny day around one o'clock, no phone call first. When the door opened, Pomfret took two very firm steps back, and Marr started talking fast. Going through Morrissey's singles, he found The Monochrome Set, a band they both loved.

The next day Morrissey phoned to say he was in. A few days later they worked up songs in Marr's rented attic in Bowdon on a TEAC four-track: 'The Hand That Rocks the Cradle', 'Suffer Little Children' and a cover of the Cookies' 'I Want a Boy for My Birthday'.

years.h: Mike Joyce auditions on magic mushrooms and gets the job
years.p: With [[Dale Hibbert|8857d5ee-fd54-46e9-bbc3-33591e11a35b]] on bass and Simon Wolstencroft sitting in, the band cut a first demo overnight at Decibel Studios. Wolstencroft didn't want to join; [[Mike Joyce|871eb71d-e0ad-4c4b-80ae-6b06dee6cabe]] did.
years.xp:
Morrissey took the demo to Factory Records. Tony Wilson wasn't interested.

By late 1982 Morrissey had picked the name, saying it was "the most ordinary name" and time ordinary folk showed their faces. He had also decided he would go by his surname alone.

years.cap: Poster for the Smiths' second gig, Portland Hotel, Manchester, November 5, 1982
years.h: First gig at the Ritz, with a friend on maracas
years.p: Supporting Blue Rondo à la Turk at a student fashion show in Manchester, the band walks on to Klaus Nomi's 'The Cold Song'. Morrissey's friend James Maker introduces them, then stays onstage with maracas and red wine.
years.xp: Maker's brief, as he told it: carte blanche, no instructions, and stay inside a chalk circle Morrissey had drawn around him. The set mixed originals with 'I Want a Boy for My Birthday'.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Smiths · The Guardian: Andy Rourke obituary
years.h: Andy Rourke takes the bass from Dale Hibbert
years.p: Marr brings in his old schoolfriend [[Andy Rourke|39ca91ba-e7b9-4e23-b0f0-1bed9d806810]]. A second demo at Drone Studios in Chorlton, with 'What Difference Does It Make?' and 'Handsome Devil', goes to EMI, who turn it down.
years.xp:
Accounts of Hibbert's exit differ. One version has him uneasy with the band's camp image; Hibbert denies that and says he never knew why he was asked to leave.

Rourke and Marr had been playing together since school in 1975, and had already shared a funk band, Freak Party, with Wolstencroft.

eras.title: A cassette for Geoff Travis
eras.text: Rough Trade began as a record shop in west London. Its new band broke inside a year, through Peel sessions, a Top of the Pops debut with flowers and a debut album that only Simple Minds kept off the top.

years.src: Wikipedia: Hand in Glove · Wikipedia: The Smiths · The Guardian: Johnny Marr interviews
yt: 'Hand in Glove' live at the Haçienda, February 1983
years.h: Geoff Travis hears a cassette and puts out 'Hand in Glove'
years.p: Marr and Rourke take their tape to [[Geoff Travis|70437714-3183-4916-947f-e5ba2154d16a]] at [[Rough Trade|4f4b0013-1704-4936-a769-e6e8a6e08ff8]] in London. The first single, with a nude male photo from Margaret Walters' The Nude Male on the sleeve, reaches No. 3 on the indie chart.
years.xp:
It never made the national Top 40, but it kept selling for the next 18 months. In 1984 Sandie Shaw covered it with Marr, Rourke and Joyce as her band, and took it to No. 27.

Travis, interviewed by Marr for the Guardian in 2009, said the record connected with "that psychic turmoil and musical nirvana" he had chased since hearing the Who as a kid.

Among the crowd at the band's second London show, at ULU, was John Walters, producer of [[John Peel|e4dec348-ad10-43b6-a2b1-c22aab890675]]'s Radio 1 show. He booked a session. Peel said you couldn't immediately tell what records they'd been listening to.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Smiths (album) · Wikipedia: The Smiths
years.h: Rough Trade scraps the first album and calls John Porter
years.p: The sessions with Troy Tate at Elephant Studios in Wapping are shelved. Porter re-records the album in Manchester and London between September and November.
years.xp:
Porter called the Tate tapes out of tune and out of time. Travis and Rough Trade wanted a new producer, and the band took Porter's offer.

Morrissey and Marr signed the Rough Trade contract on the band's behalf, and nobody discussed how the money would be divided. That silence cost a great deal later.

years.cap: Morrissey and Marr at Liverpool Polytechnic, October 1983
years.h: Sire's Seymour Stein buys Marr a 1960 Gibson ES-355
years.p: Marr had heard Stein once bought Brian Jones a guitar, and made it part of the American deal. He picked it out in a shop on 48th Street in Manhattan.

years.cap: Morrissey and Marr onstage at Liverpool Polytechnic, October 1983
years.src: The Guardian: Andy Rourke obituary · Wikipedia: The Smiths discography
years.h: 'This Charming Man' gets them into the Top 40
years.p: The second single reaches No. 25, Rourke's bassline right up front. Bass Player magazine later voted that line the 56th best of all time.

yt: 'This Charming Man' on Top of the Pops, November 24, 1983
years.h: Morrissey brings gladioli to Top of the Pops
years.p: The band's TV debut, 'This Charming Man' on BBC One. Morrissey sings it waving a bunch of gladioli, the flowers he'd keep bringing onstage.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Smiths (album) · Wikipedia: The Smiths
years.h: The Smiths stalls at No. 2 behind Simple Minds
years.p: The debut sits 33 weeks on the chart and tops the indie list. Morrissey designs the sleeve around a cropped still of Joe Dallesandro from Paul Morrissey's film Flesh.
years.xp: Tabloids claimed 'Reel Around the Fountain' and 'The Hand That Rocks the Cradle' hinted at child abuse. Earlier The Sun's Garry Bushell had said the same about the B-side 'Handsome Devil'. The band denied it flatly; Morrissey said 'Handsome Devil' had nothing to do with children.

years.h: The Smiths play Channel 4's The Tube
years.p: A full studio set on the Newcastle music show, a month after the debut album.

years.h: 'Heaven Knows I'm Miserable Now' is the first top ten hit
years.p: It reaches No. 10 and starts the band's long run with engineer and producer [[Stephen Street|47c7deb5-2e24-45ec-944e-d9d103afb312]]. Its B-side, 'Suffer Little Children', about the Moors murders, causes an uproar.
years.xp:
The grandfather of one of the murdered children heard 'Suffer Little Children' on a pub jukebox and believed the band was cashing in. After meeting Morrissey he accepted the song was sincere.

Morrissey went on to become friends with Ann West, mother of Lesley Ann Downey, who is named in the song.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Smiths · Wikipedia: The Smiths discography
years.h: 'How Soon Is Now?' starts life as a B-side
years.p: The flip of 'William, It Was Really Nothing' carries the band's most famous guitar sound. Rough Trade puts it out as an A-side in early 1985, and it reaches No. 24.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Smiths · Wikipedia: The Smiths discography
years.h: Peel and Jensen sessions become Hatful of Hollow
years.p: Singles, B-sides and radio versions in one album. It reaches No. 7, nine months after the debut.

eras.title: No meat, no monarchy, no bass player
eras.text: The second album went to No. 1 and Morrissey turned interviews into campaigns against Thatcher, the Crown and Band Aid. Behind it, the band was fighting Rough Trade in court, Marr was drinking too much, and Rourke was fired by note, or so the story goes.

years.h: Meat Is Murder goes straight to No. 1
years.p: Their only studio album to top the UK chart, with 'The Headmaster Ritual' and Rourke's funk bass on 'Barbarism Begins at Home'. Nobody in the band may be photographed eating meat.
years.xp:
The cover is a 1967 photo of US Marine Corporal Michael Wynn from Emile de Antonio's documentary In the Year of the Pig, his helmet slogan changed to the album title. Wynn later said nobody asked him and he didn't like the change.

The American pressing added 'How Soon Is Now?' to side two.

years.h: Morrissey picks fights with Thatcher, the Queen and Band Aid
years.p: Interviews become set pieces. His line on Band Aid: concern for Ethiopia is one thing, inflicting "daily torture on the people of England" another.

years.cap: The Smiths outside Salford Lads Club, Salford, 1985
years.h: Stephen Wright shoots the band outside Salford Lads Club
years.p: The four stand under the club's terracotta arches in Ordsall in rotten dark weather. The photo goes inside The Queen Is Dead and becomes one of the best-known pictures in British music.
years.xp:
The club credits the photo with keeping it open. It has hung at the National Portrait Gallery and Manchester Art Gallery, and Wright went back for the album's 40th anniversary in 2026 to photograph visitors in the same spot.

Wright remembered a basic camera and rotten dark weather.

years.h: The Queen Is Dead is finished, then held for seven months
years.p: A legal dispute with Rough Trade freezes the album completed in November 1985. Planned for February, it comes out in June.

years.big: "Andy, you have left the Smiths. Goodbye and good luck."
years.src: Wikipedia: The Smiths · The Guardian: Andy Rourke obituary
years.h: Rourke is fired over heroin, and Craig Gannon arrives
years.p: That's the Post-it Rourke said he found on his windscreen, signed Morrissey. Morrissey denied writing it. Rourke was back within two weeks.
years.xp:
Marr scouted [[Craig Gannon|856ee0fb-8378-4f59-9e42-365e8c7f7425]] of [[Aztec Camera|53578264-7436-437b-87a0-3b034a3661f0]] to cover bass, but Gannon had never played it. He stayed on as a second guitarist instead, and the Smiths were a five-piece for most of 1986.

Marr was struggling too. He later told NME he was "drinking more than I could handle" by the end of the touring.

yt: The Queen Is Dead, a film by Derek Jarman
years.h: The Queen Is Dead, with Alain Delon on the front
years.p: Recorded at Jacobs, RAK and Drone with [[Stephen Street|47c7deb5-2e24-45ec-944e-d9d103afb312]], it peaks at No. 2. In 2013 NME named it the greatest album of all time.
years.xp:
Marr used an E-mu Emulator to fake the strings on 'There Is a Light That Never Goes Out' and 'The Boy with the Thorn in His Side'. The title track opens with a sample from the 1962 film The L-Shaped Room.

Red Krayola's Mayo Thompson talked Derek Jarman into directing a short film for the songs. The sleeve's Delon still is from L'Insoumis.
play: There Is a Light That Never Goes Out

years.src: Wikipedia: The Smiths · Wikipedia: The Smiths discography
years.h: Gannon's first single with the band, 'Panic', reaches No. 11
years.p: The five-piece's first release. 'Ask', with Kirsty MacColl on backing vocals, follows in October and reaches No. 14.

years.h: Radio City is cancelled; the US tour stops in Florida
years.p: A drug arrest almost costs Rourke the North American tour; his visa comes through just in time. After St. Petersburg, Florida, Morrissey and Marr cancel the last four shows.
years.xp:
Guy Pratt had been lined up to replace Rourke. The cancelled dates included a finale at New York's Radio City Music Hall.

Wikipedia's account lists the pressures of that summer: heavy drinking and drug use by everyone but Morrissey, weak management, a band eyeing EMI over Rough Trade, and Morrissey's belief that Sire wasn't promoting them.

years.h: Gannon hears second-hand that he's out
years.p: After the October UK tour he simply isn't called to rehearsals. Friend Ivor Perry tells him Travis said he was no longer in the band.
years.xp: Gannon played on seven studio tracks: 'Panic', 'Ask', 'The Draize Train', 'Golden Lights', 'Half a Person', 'London' and 'You Just Haven't Earned It Yet, Baby'.

years.h: Brixton Academy turns out to be the last show
years.p: An anti-apartheid benefit in south London, with Gannon gone and the original four onstage.

eras.title: Smiths to split
eras.text: The band signed to EMI and made the album both songwriters would later call their favourite. Then an NME headline did what the year's other pressures had been threatening to do.

years.src: Wikipedia: Strangeways, Here We Come · Wikipedia: The Smiths
years.h: Strangeways opens on piano and has no guitar on track one
years.p: Recorded at the Wool Hall near Bath, with an EMI deal signed for what came next. Marr plays keyboards across it, wanting away from the jangle; he and Morrissey both name it their favourite Smiths album.
years.xp: Marr told NME every label had come calling: "It was small-talk, bribes, the whole number. I really enjoyed it." Signing to a major drew criticism from fans and parts of the press.
play: A Rush and a Push and the Land Is Ours

years.big: "I didn't form a group to perform Cilla Black songs."
q: It's what split the band up.
Johnny Marr, 2016, on managing the band
years.src: Wikipedia: The Smiths · NME: Johnny Marr
years.h: Marr quits after an NME story headlined 'Smiths to Split'
years.p: Marr in 1992, on Morrissey's taste for '60s covers. He wrongly believed Morrissey had planted Danny Kelly's NME piece, and left.
years.xp:
Marr told NME at the time he wanted wider musical scope, not that the friendship had snapped. In 2016 he told the Guardian he had been left running the band after a string of managers went: "I haven't met anyone who thinks a major rock group should be managed by the 23-year-old guitar player."

Former Easterhouse guitarist Ivor Perry tried out with the other three, cutting an early 'Bengali in Platforms'. Perry said "it was like they wanted another Johnny Marr"; the sessions ended with Morrissey running out of the studio.

years.src: Wikipedia: Strangeways, Here We Come · Wikipedia: The Smiths
years.h: Strangeways comes out after the band is gone
years.p: No. 2 in the UK and No. 55 in the US, the Smiths' best American showing. The cover is Richard Davalos from East of Eden, with James Dean cropped out.
play: Last Night I Dreamt That Somebody Loved Me

eras.title: Forty, forty, ten, ten
eras.text: Morrissey went straight to No. 1 on his own and Marr joined everybody from The The to New Order's Bernard Sumner. Then the rhythm section asked what happened to their share, and a judge answered.

years.h: Morrissey's Viva Hate goes to No. 1
years.p: Made with Stephen Street and [[Vini Reilly|f639c53e-c709-407f-9711-de495461f28d]] of [[The Durutti Column|aaddb5e3-f8a5-4a9d-8674-f885112ecf0e]]. Rourke and Joyce play on Morrissey singles in 1988 and 1989; Marr forms [[Electronic|3cdb360e-d0a2-459f-92f6-f0f28e62127d]] with [[Bernard Sumner|6fa2e161-200e-475a-8492-3755594581f9]] and [[Neil Tennant|8dac8c65-bcb3-4730-b82a-58727ea44e41]].

years.h: Joyce and Rourke sue Morrissey and Marr
years.p: They argue they were equal partners owed 25 per cent, not the 10 they got. Rourke, in debt, settles for £83,000 and 10 per cent of royalties.

years.h: The High Court sides with Mike Joyce
years.p: Judge Weeks on Morrissey, after a seven-day hearing. Joyce gets around £1 million in back royalties and 25 per cent from then on.
years.xp:
Joyce's barrister said the drummer and bassist had been treated as "readily replaceable as the parts in a lawnmower". Marr's counsel admitted that 13 years on, nobody could pinpoint when the 40:40:10:10 split began. Nothing had been written down, which Marr later said he regretted.

The judge found Marr "willing to embroider his evidence". Morrissey appealed; the Court of Appeal dismissed it in November 1998. Rourke was declared bankrupt in 1999.

eras.title: Every offer refused
eras.text: Promoters kept naming bigger numbers and the answer kept being no, though not always for the same reasons. Rourke moved to New York and kept playing with Marr until the end.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Smiths · The Guardian: Andy Rourke obituary
years.h: Marr and Rourke play 'How Soon Is Now?' for Manchester v Cancer
years.p: Rourke helped set up the benefit series, and Marr's band, the Healers, played it. The two did the song together again at Lollapalooza Brazil in 2014.

years.h: Morrissey turns down $5 million to reunite at Coachella
years.p: "Money doesn't come into it," he said; Marr was the one who ended it. That year he also said he'd rather eat his own testicles than reform the band.
years.xp: In September 2008, with Marr remastering the catalogue, the two met in Manchester and talked for four days about reforming, without Joyce. The conversation stopped while Marr was touring Mexico with [[The Cribs|a3a92047-be1c-4f3e-8960-c4f8570984df]], and he didn't hear from Morrissey again until December 2010.

years.h: Andy Rourke dies at 59
years.p: Rourke died of pancreatic cancer; he had lived in New York since 2009. His last performance was with Marr's band at Madison Square Garden in September 2022.
years.xp:
Marr announced the death and called him a "beautiful soul" and a "supremely gifted musician". After the Smiths, Rourke played with Sinéad O'Connor, The Pretenders and [[Ian Brown|182d5d8a-94c7-4ef4-8222-a1838353a37b]], and formed Freebass with [[Peter Hook|73e7c483-9f3e-4a72-a359-582452fbaeac]] and Mani.

He once summed up his approach to bass: "I tried to do a tune within a tune."

years.cap: Marr onstage at Audley End, Saffron Walden, August 1, 2024
years.h: Marr answers a reunion question with a picture of Nigel Farage
years.p: Morrissey said he'd accepted a lucrative 2025 tour offer and Marr hadn't replied. Marr declined, then disputed Morrissey's claims about the band's trademark.
years.xp:
Marr said he registered the Smiths trademark in his own name after a third party tried to use it in 2018 and Morrissey didn't respond, while agreeing to share it with him.

In 2025 Joyce said a reunion without Rourke was impossible, though he wouldn't object to Morrissey and Marr playing together.
